children: The government is working to list India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) by March 2027, with the public offering expected to be completed before the end of the current financial year, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Arunish Chawla told CNBC-TV18 exclusively on Monday, November 16.

“We are on the job. We are hoping to complete it before March in the current financial year,” Chawla said in an interview with CNBC-TV18, adding that the proceeds from the listing would count towards the government's capital receipts for FY27.

The proposed IPO is part of the government's broader disinvestment and asset monetisation pipeline. The Centre has set a capital receipts target of ₹80,000 crore for the current financial year, which includes proceeds from asset sales and monetisation. Chawla said the government had already achieved ₹62,000 crore through these mechanisms.
“We will achieve our yearly target of ₹80,000 crore for this investment, and hopefully exceed it,” he said.
Chawla did not disclose the likely issue size or other details of the IIFCL IPO in the interview.

IIFCL is a wholly owned government company established in 2006 to provide long-term financial assistance to viable infrastructure projects in India. It is registered with the Reserve Bank of India as a non-banking financial company - infrastructure finance company (NBFC-IFC).

The company provides financing across infrastructure sectors, with priority given to public-private partnership (PPP) projects. Its lending and financing activities include direct lending, takeout finance, refinancing and credit enhancement.
IIFCL's role is to support infrastructure projects that require long-term funding, including in sectors such as roads, bridges, railways, ports, airports, power and urban infrastructure.
The IIFCL listing is among several transactions the government is pursuing as part of its capital receipts program.
Chawla also said the government is looking at the listing of South Eastern Coalfields Limited, another subsidiary of Coal India, in the coming months.
“We are hoping, you know, in another six months, we will come up with another listing, another issue, and investors should look forward,” he said.
The government is currently focused on the initial public offering of Mahanadi Coalfields, while the South Eastern Coalfields listing is expected to follow.

Chawla said the Centre is reviewing its remaining offer-for-sale pipeline on an asset-by-asset basis, taking into account market conditions, but remains confident of meeting its annual capital receipts target.

title: Exclusive: IIFCL IPO likely by March 2027, says DIPAM Secretary Arunish Chawla
